purpose: machine-readable ontology for understanding-level explanation of how large language models work as concrete explanatory work-units: representation (tokenization, embeddings, vectors, similarity, sequence/position), the transformer (self-attention, layers, next-token prediction, context window), learning phases (pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, preference tuning and what each changes), inference (sampling/decoding, prompting/in-context learning, retrieval-augmented generation), an end-to-end inference trace, and the intrinsic limits, scaling, evaluation, interpretability, and behavioral-alignment caveats that follow; a subdomain node of Computing & How LLMs Work (Foundations) for a knowledge-searcher meta-KB, kept at literacy altitude with the engineering of building/fine-tuning/orchestrating LLM systems deferred to a sibling subdomain.
assumptions: How LLMs Work is modeled as a subdomain of Computing & How LLMs Work (Foundations).
Nodes are concrete, evaluable explanatory work-units (explain tokenization, explain attention, explain a learning phase, trace an inference pass), not generic 'AI' topics.

This is the conceptual 'how it works' layer at literacy/understanding altitude; the engineering of building, fine-tuning, serving, and orchestrating LLM systems lives in a sibling subdomain and is excluded.
No observed dataset or experimental/benchmark evidence is supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors.
Scope follows Jurafsky & Martin 'Speech and Language Processing', Tunstall/von Werra/Wolf 'Natural Language Processing with Transformers', and the transformer literature.
exclusions: Engineering of building, fine-tuning (LoRA/PEFT pipelines), serving, and orchestrating LLM systems (sibling subdomain).
Training infrastructure, data pipelines, distributed training, and inference-serving optimization.
Prompt-engineering recipes and agent/tool-orchestration patterns as build products.
Detailed architecture math derivations (attention complexity proofs, exact positional-encoding formulas) beyond the conceptual layer.

competency_questions.question: At what altitude should an LLM explanation sit, and what is deferred to the build subdomain?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SCOPE_LITERACY_FRAME yields scope and excluded-build list

competency_questions.question: How does raw text become numbers the model can process?
How is 'related meaning' represented and computed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EMBEDDINGS_VECTORS and VECTOR_SIMILARITY define vector proximity

competency_questions.question: What does self-attention compute and why did it replace recurrence?
How do stacked transformer layers turn attention into a working model?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TRANSFORMER_BLOCK and SELF_ATTENTION describe block and depth

competency_questions.question: What is the model trained to do and how is text generated?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NEXT_TOKEN_PREDICTION and DECODING_SAMPLING describe objective and decoding

competency_questions.question: What is the context window and what happens at its limit?
How can a model use fresh or private knowledge without retraining?
What are the learning phases and how do they sequence?
What does each training phase change about the model?
How does the input (prompt) steer the model and how do decoding settings change output?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROMPTING and DECODING_SAMPLING link input/settings to output

competency_questions.question: How do all the parts fit into one generation pass?
Why does a confident model still produce false, outdated, or unexplained answers?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EMERGENT_LIMITS ties limits to mechanisms; INTERPRETABILITY_LIMITS caveats explanations

competency_questions.question: How should capability and scaling claims be read critically?

glossary.definition: a subword unit of text produced by the tokenizer that the model actually processes
a dense vector that represents a token so meaning becomes geometry
a mechanism where each token weights and mixes information from other tokens via query/key/value
the objective of producing a probability distribution over the vocabulary for the next token
the bounded number of tokens the model can attend to at once
large-scale self-supervised next-token learning that gives general knowledge and language ability
optimizing the model toward human-preferred responses (RLHF/DPO)
a decoding parameter that scales the next-token distribution to control randomness
fetching external passages into context so answers can use external/fresh knowledge
fluent, confident model output that is factually false

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from standard LLM/NLP literature (Jurafsky & Martin 'Speech and Language Processing'; Tunstall, von Werra & Wolf 'Natural Language Processing with Transformers'; Vaswani et al. 'Attention Is All You Need') and teaching practice; no measured dataset supplied.
does_not_support: observed model accuracy or hallucination rates
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible
capability/limit claims shift across models and versions

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Fix the explanation altitude to literacy/understanding of how LLMs work and explicitly defer engineering build mechanics to a sibling subdomain.

included: what counts as an explanatory work-unit

contradictors: engineer who jumps to build mechanics before the concept is clear
inputs: a concrete LLM behavior to explain

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the audience or the build/understand boundary is restated, changing what is in scope

pros.claim: a fixed altitude keeps explanations conceptual and prevents drift into engineering
pros.example: explaining attention without GPU kernel details

pros.claim: an explicit defer-list removes overlap with the build/orchestration subdomain
pros.example: sending LoRA fine-tuning steps to the engineering KB

cons.claim: too strict a boundary can omit mechanism a learner needs
cons.example: refusing to mention softmax when explaining next-token choice

failure_modes: altitude too abstract to be falsifiable
acceptance_tests: scope statement names the audience and the understand-vs-build boundary
every later node fits the literacy altitude
revisit_triggers: overlap with the build subdomain is detected

nodes.definition: Explain how raw text is split into tokens (subword units) by a learned tokenizer before the model sees it, and why token boundaries matter.
contradictors: belief that the model reads characters or whole words directly

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a learner asks why token counts differ from word counts or why rare words split

pros.claim: subword tokens balance vocabulary size against handling rare/unseen words
pros.example: 'tokenization' splitting into 'token'+'ization'

pros.claim: token framing explains context limits and per-token billing
pros.example: a long word costing several tokens

cons.claim: token boundaries are non-obvious and cause counting/arithmetic confusion
cons.example: model miscounting letters because they span tokens

acceptance_tests: explanation states tokens are subword units not words
a worked example shows a word splitting into multiple tokens

nodes.definition: Explain how each token id is mapped to a dense vector (embedding) so meaning becomes geometry the model can compute over.

excluded: specific embedding algorithms as build steps

contradictors: belief that words carry meaning as discrete symbols only
outputs: intuition that nearby vectors mean related tokens

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a learner asks how text becomes numbers or what an embedding 'means'

pros.claim: vectors let semantic relationships be computed as distances/directions
pros.example: king-man+woman lands near queen

pros.claim: a shared vector space is what makes similarity search and RAG possible
pros.example: matching a query vector to passage vectors

cons.claim: embeddings are not human-interpretable axis-by-axis
cons.example: no single dimension cleanly equals 'gender'

failure_modes: treating one dimension as one concept
conflating token embeddings with final contextual vectors
acceptance_tests: explanation shows token-id to vector mapping
relatedness is described as vector proximity

nodes.definition: Explain how closeness between vectors (cosine/dot similarity) operationalizes 'related meaning' and underlies search and attention.
contradictors: belief that keyword overlap equals semantic match

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a learner asks how the model 'knows' two phrases are related

pros.claim: cosine similarity gives a concrete, computable notion of relatedness
pros.example: ranking passages by closeness to a query vector

pros.claim: the same idea reappears inside attention as scaled dot products
pros.example: attention scoring keys against a query

cons.claim: high similarity is not the same as truth or relevance
cons.example: a fluent but wrong passage scoring high

acceptance_tests: explanation names a concrete similarity metric
links similarity to both search and attention

nodes.definition: Explain how order is injected (positional encoding) so a set of token vectors becomes an ordered sequence the model can reason over.
contradictors: belief that transformers are inherently order-aware without position signals
outputs: intuition for why order is added

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a learner asks why word order changes meaning if attention sees all tokens at once

pros.claim: position signals explain why 'dog bites man' differs from 'man bites dog'
pros.example: reordering flips meaning despite same tokens

pros.claim: position encoding connects directly to context-window length limits
pros.example: longer positions stressing extrapolation

cons.claim: positional schemes are an implementation detail learners can over-index on
cons.example: debating rotary vs absolute before grasping why order is needed

failure_modes: conflating position encoding with the attention mechanism itself
acceptance_tests: explanation states order is added explicitly
a reorder example changes meaning
revisit_triggers: positional scheme or context length assumptions change

nodes.definition: Explain self-attention: each token forms a query and compares it against keys to weight and mix values, letting tokens gather relevant context.
contradictors: belief that recurrence or convolution is required to model context
outputs: intuition for how tokens attend to each other

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a learner asks what attention actually computes or why it replaced recurrence

pros.claim: attention lets any token directly use any other token's information
pros.example: a pronoun attending to its antecedent far back

pros.claim: parallel attention is why transformers train efficiently on long context
pros.example: scoring all token pairs at once

cons.claim: full attention cost grows with sequence length, bounding context
cons.example: quadratic scaling pressuring window size

failure_modes: explaining attention as mere keyword matching
acceptance_tests: explanation names query/key/value and the weighting step
a long-range dependency example is given
multi-head is mentioned as parallel views
revisit_triggers: a new attention variant is referenced
context-window or cost claims are revised

nodes.definition: Explain the transformer block (attention + feed-forward with residuals and normalization) and how stacking many blocks builds abstraction.
contradictors: belief that a single attention layer is the whole model

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a learner asks what the rest of a transformer layer does besides attention

pros.claim: residuals + FFN per block are what make deep stacks trainable and expressive
pros.example: gradients flowing through skip connections

pros.claim: depth intuition explains emergent abstraction across layers
pros.example: early layers syntax, later layers semantics

cons.claim: layer internals are not cleanly interpretable feature-by-feature
cons.example: no guarantee a layer learns a named concept

failure_modes: reducing the block to attention only
acceptance_tests: explanation includes FFN, residual, and normalization
depth is linked to abstraction
revisit_triggers: architecture variant or normalization scheme changes

nodes.definition: Explain that an LLM is trained to predict the next token, producing a probability distribution over the vocabulary at each position.
contradictors: belief that the model 'looks up' answers rather than predicting tokens
outputs: intuition that generation is repeated prediction

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a learner asks what the model is actually optimizing or how text is generated

pros.claim: next-token prediction unifies training and generation in one objective
pros.example: both learning and inference predict the next token

pros.claim: the probability distribution is the hook for sampling and temperature
pros.example: top tokens reweighted before choosing

cons.claim: a fluent prediction objective rewards plausibility, not truth
cons.example: a confident, well-formed but false continuation

failure_modes: claiming the model retrieves stored answers
acceptance_tests: explanation states the model outputs a distribution over the vocabulary
generation is described as repeated next-token sampling

nodes.definition: Explain the context window: the bounded span of tokens the model can attend to at once, and the consequences of its limits.
contradictors: belief that the model remembers the whole conversation indefinitely

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a learner asks why the model 'forgets' earlier text or hits length limits

pros.claim: the window concept explains forgetting, truncation, and why RAG/chunking exist
pros.example: old turns dropping out of a long chat

pros.claim: length-cost scaling motivates prompt economy and retrieval
pros.example: trimming context to fit and cut cost

cons.claim: users overestimate effective use of long windows (lost-in-the-middle)
cons.example: mid-context facts being underused

acceptance_tests: explanation states the window is finite in tokens
describes a concrete consequence of exceeding it

nodes.definition: Explain pretraining: large-scale self-supervised next-token learning over broad text that gives the model its general knowledge and language ability.

included: what general capability comes from here

contradictors: belief that the model is explicitly taught facts one by one

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a learner asks where the model's knowledge comes from or what a base model is

pros.claim: pretraining explains broad competence without task-specific labels
pros.example: predicting next tokens across the open web

pros.claim: it grounds the idea of a knowledge cutoff and stale facts
pros.example: no events after the training data end

cons.claim: pretraining absorbs biases and errors present in the corpus
cons.example: repeating a common online misconception

failure_modes: ignoring that the base model is not instruction-following
acceptance_tests: explanation states pretraining is self-supervised next-token learning
links it to knowledge cutoff and base-model behavior

nodes.definition: Explain supervised fine-tuning (instruction tuning): training the base model on curated input-output demonstrations so it follows instructions.

included: turning a base model into an assistant

contradictors: belief that a base model is already a chat assistant
outputs: intuition for behavior vs new knowledge

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a learner asks how a raw model becomes a helpful instruction-follower

pros.claim: SFT explains the jump from text-completer to instruction-follower
pros.example: base model rambling vs assistant answering

pros.claim: clarifies that SFT mostly shapes behavior/format, less new world knowledge
pros.example: learning to answer, not new facts

cons.claim: SFT can overfit demonstration style and narrow behavior
cons.example: mimicking a narrow answer template

failure_modes: claiming SFT injects large new knowledge
acceptance_tests: explanation distinguishes SFT from pretraining
states SFT mainly changes instruction-following behavior

nodes.definition: Explain preference tuning (RLHF/DPO): optimizing the model toward human-preferred responses using a reward or preference signal.
contradictors: belief that helpfulness/safety emerge automatically from pretraining

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a learner asks how models are made helpful, harmless, or aligned to preferences

pros.claim: preference tuning explains tone, refusals, and helpfulness beyond SFT
pros.example: declining a harmful request politely

pros.claim: DPO/RLHF framing clarifies optimization toward judged-better outputs
pros.example: ranking two answers to teach preference

cons.claim: preference optimization can induce sycophancy or over-refusal
cons.example: agreeing with a user to seem helpful

acceptance_tests: explanation names a preference signal (reward or comparison)
distinguishes preference tuning from SFT and pretraining

nodes.definition: Synthesize what each learning phase changes: pretraining gives knowledge, SFT gives instruction-following, preference tuning shapes helpful/safe behavior.
contradictors: belief that one phase explains all model behavior
inputs: descriptions of pretraining, SFT, and preference tuning
outputs: intuition for which phase to blame for a behavior

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a learner asks which training phase caused a specific capability or quirk

pros.claim: a phase map lets behaviors be attributed to the right training stage
pros.example: blaming refusals on preference tuning not pretraining

pros.claim: it prevents the common error of crediting all behavior to 'the training'
pros.example: separating knowledge from instruction-following

cons.claim: phase effects overlap and are not perfectly separable
cons.example: knowledge also subtly shaped during SFT

failure_modes: over-crisp attribution of behavior to one phase
acceptance_tests: map attributes knowledge, instruction-following, and behavior to the correct phases
at least one quirk is attributed correctly
revisit_triggers: any phase's described effect is revised
a new training stage is added

nodes.definition: Explain decoding: how the next-token distribution is turned into text via greedy/sampling, with temperature and top-p controlling randomness.
contradictors: belief that the model has one fixed deterministic answer
outputs: intuition for how settings change output style

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a learner asks why outputs vary or what temperature/top-p actually do

pros.claim: decoding settings concretely explain output variability and creativity
pros.example: high temperature giving more varied wording

pros.claim: connects directly to the next-token distribution learners just met
pros.example: reweighting then sampling the top tokens

cons.claim: high randomness raises incoherence/hallucination risk
cons.example: temperature too high producing nonsense

acceptance_tests: explanation links a setting (temperature/top-p) to an output effect
contrasts greedy with sampling
revisit_triggers: default decoding parameters or interfaces change

nodes.definition: Explain prompting and in-context learning: how the input text steers the model, including instructions, examples, and context, without changing weights.
contradictors: belief that prompting retrains or permanently changes the model
outputs: intuition that prompting conditions, not retrains

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a learner asks why wording changes answers or what in-context learning is

pros.claim: prompting explains huge behavior changes with no weight updates
pros.example: few-shot examples improving format adherence

pros.claim: in-context learning clarifies that examples condition, not train
pros.example: the model imitating provided examples

cons.claim: prompt sensitivity makes behavior brittle and hard to predict
cons.example: a trivial rewording flipping the answer

failure_modes: claiming prompts permanently change the model
acceptance_tests: explanation states prompting conditions without changing weights
gives a few-shot vs zero-shot contrast

nodes.definition: Explain retrieval-augmented generation: fetching relevant external passages and placing them in context so answers can use up-to-date or private knowledge.
contradictors: belief that the model must be retrained to learn new facts

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a learner asks how models use fresh or private knowledge without retraining

pros.claim: RAG explains using current/private data without retraining the model
pros.example: answering from a freshly retrieved document

pros.claim: it ties similarity, context window, and prompting into one applied pattern
pros.example: embedding a query to fetch then ground

cons.claim: retrieval errors propagate; wrong passages cause confident wrong answers
cons.example: grounding on an irrelevant retrieved chunk

acceptance_tests: explanation states retrieve-then-place-in-context
links RAG to knowledge cutoff and grounding

nodes.definition: Trace one end-to-end inference pass: text -> tokens -> embeddings -> transformer layers -> next-token logits -> decoding -> text.
contradictors: belief that the model 'thinks' outside this pipeline
outputs: a step-by-step trace of one generation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a learner asks to see how all the parts fit into one generation

pros.claim: an end-to-end trace consolidates isolated concepts into one mental model
pros.example: following one token from text to output

pros.claim: it exposes where each earlier concept actually acts
pros.example: seeing decoding act on the final distribution

cons.claim: a single trace can imply more determinism/clarity than reality
cons.example: hiding sampling randomness in a clean diagram

failure_modes: leaving the pipeline as disconnected parts
acceptance_tests: trace covers tokenize, embed, attend, predict, decode in order
each step references the right upstream node
revisit_triggers: any upstream concept's explanation is revised

nodes.definition: Explain core limitations that follow from how LLMs work: hallucination, knowledge cutoff, brittleness, and unreliable self-reported reasoning.
contradictors: belief that confident, fluent output implies correctness
outputs: intuition linking each limit to a mechanism

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a learner asks why a confident model still produces false or outdated answers

pros.claim: tying limits to mechanisms makes them predictable, not mysterious
pros.example: hallucination from a plausibility objective

pros.claim: the cutoff and brittleness explanations set correct expectations
pros.example: model unaware of last week's news

cons.claim: limits are probabilistic and shift across models/versions
cons.example: a failure on one model not another

acceptance_tests: each limit is linked to a generating mechanism
an example of fluent-but-false output is given
revisit_triggers: model capability/limit claims change across versions

nodes.definition: Explain scaling intuition: how more parameters, data, and compute tend to improve capability, and the contested idea of emergent abilities.
contradictors: belief that scale alone guarantees correctness or reasoning
outputs: a calibrated view of emergence claims

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a learner asks whether bigger models are simply better or 'understand'

pros.claim: scaling intuition explains why capability rose with model size
pros.example: quality jumps between model generations

pros.claim: a calibrated emergence view avoids both hype and dismissal
pros.example: treating 'emergence' as measurement-dependent

cons.claim: emergence is contested and often a metric artifact
cons.example: apparent jumps vanishing under smooth metrics

acceptance_tests: scaling is described over parameters/data/compute
emergence is flagged as contested

nodes.definition: Explain at a literacy level how LLM capability is judged: perplexity, benchmarks, and human/LLM evaluation, and why scores can mislead.
contradictors: belief that a single benchmark score fully captures capability

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a learner asks how to read or trust an LLM capability/benchmark claim

pros.claim: eval literacy lets learners critically read capability claims
pros.example: spotting benchmark contamination

pros.claim: perplexity and benchmark caveats temper marketing numbers
pros.example: a high score on a leaked test set

cons.claim: benchmarks drift and can be gamed or contaminated
cons.example: train-test overlap inflating scores

acceptance_tests: explanation names at least one eval method and one caveat
links a metric to what it does/doesn't show

nodes.definition: Explain at a literacy level what is and isn't inspectable inside an LLM: weights/activations exist but mapping them to human concepts is hard and partial.

included: activations and attention as weak explanations

contradictors: belief that attention weights or chain-of-thought are faithful explanations
outputs: a calibrated view of model transparency
intuition for why explanations are partial

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a learner asks whether we can see why a model gave an answer

pros.claim: setting transparency expectations prevents over-trusting explanations
pros.example: not treating attention as a faithful reason

pros.claim: it clarifies that a model's stated reasoning may not be its actual process
pros.example: plausible but post-hoc rationale

cons.claim: the field is young; claims about interpretability shift quickly
cons.example: a probing result not replicating

acceptance_tests: explanation distinguishes inspectable internals from faithful explanation
notes self-reported reasoning is not guaranteed faithful

nodes.definition: Explain the behavioral surface produced by preference tuning: assistant persona, refusals, hedging, and helpfulness, and that it is shaped not intrinsic.
contradictors: belief that the assistant persona is an inherent property of the network
outputs: a view of behavior as shaped by tuning
intuition for why models refuse or hedge

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a learner asks why the model refuses, hedges, or has a consistent persona

pros.claim: framing persona/refusals as tuned behavior demystifies the assistant
pros.example: a refusal tracing to preference tuning

pros.claim: it separates surface behavior from underlying capability
pros.example: a capable model still refusing by policy

cons.claim: behavior varies by provider/version and can be inconsistent
cons.example: different refusal behavior across models

acceptance_tests: explanation attributes refusals/persona to preference tuning
notes behavior is provider/version dependent
revisit_triggers: alignment/safety behavior norms change across versions

edges.why_related: the scope altitude decides how tokenization is explained (concept not build)
tokens are the units that get mapped to embeddings
similarity is defined over the embedding vectors
position info is added to token embeddings to form a sequence
attention scores are similarity (scaled dot product) between query and keys
attention mixes position-aware token vectors
the block wraps attention with FFN/residual/norm
stacked blocks produce the representation the prediction head uses
the window bounds how many tokens the objective conditions on
attention cost over token pairs is what bounds practical window length
pretraining is the objective applied at scale
SFT starts from the pretrained base model
preference tuning typically follows SFT
the map needs pretraining's contribution defined
the map needs SFT's contribution defined
the map needs preference tuning's contribution defined
decoding operates on the next-token distribution
prompting conditions the next-token distribution via context
the window bounds how much prompt/context can steer the model
retrieval ranks passages by vector similarity to the query
retrieved passages must fit the context window
RAG places retrieved text into the prompt/context
window limits cause forgetting/truncation failures
a plausibility objective causes hallucination
a fixed pretraining corpus causes knowledge cutoff and absorbed bias
high-randomness decoding raises incoherence/hallucination
scaling pretraining data/params/compute drives capability trends
scaling improves capability yet does not remove core limits, creating an expectation tension
edges.resolution_rule: present scaling gains and persistent limits together; neither dominates the other claim

edges.why_related: perplexity is the objective measured on held-out text
edges.risk_of_conflict: eval with no link to objective

edges.why_related: attention weights tempt but do not provide faithful explanations
edges.resolution_rule: attention is not a faithful explanation

edges.why_related: layer internals resist clean concept mapping
edges.resolution_rule: layer internals are only partially interpretable

edges.why_related: preference tuning produces refusals/persona/hedging
preference tuning can introduce sycophancy/over-refusal
edges.resolution_rule: tuning can create new behavioral limits

edges.why_related: the pipeline ends at decoding to text
the pipeline starts at tokenization
attention is the core middle step of the trace
sampling randomness makes single-run eval noisy, tensioning reproducible scoring
edges.resolution_rule: hold decoding fixed (greedy/seed) when measuring capability

edges.why_related: prompt sensitivity is itself a brittleness limit, tensioning 'just prompt better' with reliability
edges.resolution_rule: treat prompt brittleness as a real limit, not only a fix

edges.why_related: RAG mitigates cutoff yet adds retrieval-error failure modes, a tradeoff
edges.resolution_rule: present RAG as mitigation that adds its own failure mode

edges.why_related: embeddings invite per-dimension interpretation that interpretability limits warn against
edges.resolution_rule: embeddings are not axis-interpretable; defer to interpretability caveats

conflict_axes.trigger: an explanation drifts from 'how it works' into how to build/train/serve it
resolution_order: route build detail to the engineering subdomain
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the literacy altitude dominates; include only the mechanism needed to understand behavior, defer build steps
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a node turns into a training/serving how-to
conflict_axes.example: explaining attention without diving into kernel optimization

conflict_axes.trigger: a fluent, confident output is mistaken for a correct one
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: correctness framing dominates: never present fluency as evidence of truth
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a confident false answer is treated as authoritative

conflict_axes.trigger: sampling randomness is wanted for variety but breaks reproducible scoring
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: for evaluation, determinism dominates (greedy/seed); for open generation, controlled sampling is allowed
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: capability is judged from a single sampled run
conflict_axes.example: benchmarking with temperature>0 and one sample

conflict_axes.trigger: a behavior change is attributed to prompting when it actually requires training (or vice versa)
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: mechanism dominates: prompting conditions without weight change; training changes weights
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: prompting is claimed to permanently teach the model

conflict_axes.trigger: RAG is presented as eliminating hallucination rather than shifting the failure mode
resolution_order: note retrieval errors create new failures
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: balanced: RAG reduces some errors and adds retrieval-dependent ones; neither side is absolute
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: RAG is claimed to guarantee correctness
conflict_axes.example: grounding confidently on an irrelevant retrieved chunk

conflict_axes.trigger: scaling is presented as removing fundamental limits like hallucination or cutoff
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: calibration dominates: report gains and persistent limits together; avoid both hype and dismissal
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: scale is claimed to yield understanding or remove hallucination
conflict_axes.example: assuming the next bigger model cannot hallucinate

conflict_axes.trigger: attention weights or chain-of-thought are presented as faithful explanations of the model's reasoning
resolution_order: show attention is informative not faithful
flag stated reasoning as possibly post-hoc
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: faithfulness skepticism dominates: treat internal signals and self-explanations as partial, not ground truth
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a model's stated reason is taken as its actual mechanism
conflict_axes.example: trusting a high attention weight as 'the reason'

conflict_axes.trigger: the assistant persona/refusals are treated as intrinsic network properties rather than tuned behavior
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: shaped-behavior framing dominates: refusals/persona are tuned, not inherent
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: persona is claimed to be an emergent intrinsic trait
conflict_axes.example: saying the model 'is' cautious rather than 'was tuned to be'

edge_cases.trigger: tokens are explained as whole words
edge_cases.failure_mode: learner mispredicts token counts and splitting behavior
edge_cases.detection_method: check the explanation states tokens are subword units with a splitting example

edge_cases.trigger: a single embedding dimension is described as one human concept
edge_cases.detection_method: check no claim maps one dimension to one named concept
resolution: describe meaning as distributed across dimensions

edge_cases.trigger: attention weights are presented as faithful explanations
edge_cases.example: 'the model attended here, so that is why'
edge_cases.detection_method: check attention is called informative-not-faithful where used as explanation
resolution: route strong interpretability claims to human review

edge_cases.trigger: a fluent confident answer is treated as correct
edge_cases.detection_method: check the objective-rewards-plausibility caveat is present and fluency is separated from truth

edge_cases.trigger: the model is described as remembering everything indefinitely
edge_cases.example: expecting a 200-page chat to be fully retained
edge_cases.detection_method: check the window is stated as finite with a truncation/forgetting consequence

edge_cases.trigger: prompting is described as retraining or permanently changing the model
edge_cases.detection_method: check prompting is stated to condition without weight change
resolution: state no weight update in prompting

edge_cases.trigger: RAG is claimed to eliminate hallucination
edge_cases.example: trusting an answer grounded on a wrong passage
edge_cases.detection_method: check RAG is framed as mitigation that adds retrieval-error failure modes

edge_cases.trigger: all behavior is attributed to one training phase
edge_cases.detection_method: check behaviors map to the correct phase per the phase map

edge_cases.trigger: scaling is claimed to remove fundamental limits
edge_cases.detection_method: check gains and persistent limits are presented together
resolution: state which limits persist with scale

edge_cases.trigger: capability is judged from one benchmark number or one sampled run
edge_cases.detection_method: check at least one eval caveat (contamination/variance) accompanies any score

edge_cases.trigger: a node turns into a build/training/serving how-to
edge_cases.failure_mode: scope drift and overlap with the engineering subdomain
edge_cases.detection_method: check each node stays at understanding altitude and defers build steps
resolution: route build detail to the engineering subdomain

workflow.objective: fix the understanding-level altitude and the build/understand boundary
entry_criteria: a learner question or LLM behavior to explain
acceptance_tests: scope names audience and understand-vs-build boundary
workflow.do_first_because: the literacy altitude is the highest-coupling foundation every later explanation inherits

workflow.objective: explain how text becomes ordered vectors with a notion of similarity
acceptance_tests: tokens are subword
text->vector path shown
similarity defined
order added
workflow.do_first_because: representation must precede the transformer because attention operates on these vectors

workflow.objective: explain self-attention and the stacked transformer block
acceptance_tests: query/key/value named
block includes FFN/residual/norm
workflow.do_first_because: attention is the central mechanism the rest of the model and limits depend on

workflow.objective: explain the next-token objective and the context window limit
acceptance_tests: distribution-over-vocab stated
window stated finite
workflow.do_first_because: the objective defines what the model does and seeds learning phases, inference, and limits

workflow.objective: explain pretraining, SFT, preference tuning, and what each changes
acceptance_tests: each phase distinguished
phase map attributes knowledge/behavior correctly
workflow.do_first_because: phases build on the objective and must be ordered pretrain->SFT->preference to avoid attribution errors

workflow.objective: explain decoding, prompting/in-context learning, and retrieval-augmented generation
acceptance_tests: temperature/top-p linked to output
prompting framed as conditioning
RAG framed as grounding
workflow.do_first_because: inference reuses the objective/window and is needed before the end-to-end synthesis

workflow.objective: trace one end-to-end inference pass connecting all parts
acceptance_tests: trace covers tokenize->embed->attend->predict->decode
workflow.do_first_because: synthesis must follow the parts it connects to avoid forward references

workflow.objective: explain intrinsic limits and the tuned behavioral surface, tied to mechanisms
acceptance_tests: each limit linked to a mechanism
fluency separated from truth
workflow.do_first_because: limits are high-risk because mis-stating them causes over-trust; they need mechanism grounding and review

workflow.objective: calibrate expectations on scaling, evaluation, and interpretability
acceptance_tests: scaling marked contested
eval caveat present
interpretability framed partial
workflow.do_first_because: calibration depends on the limits being defined and tempers capability claims before release

workflow.objective: run validation, resolve defects, and gate hard-lock on review
acceptance_tests: validator passes
high-risk nodes reviewed
workflow.do_first_because: hard-lock may only follow dependency, validation, and human-review gates

priority_rationale.notes: similarity reused by attention and RAG
central mechanism the model and limits depend on
wraps attention into the trainable block
objective at scale; base for SFT
attributes behavior to the right phase
conditions the distribution; needed by RAG
applied pattern joining similarity, window, prompting

dominance_rules.trigger: a confident answer is wanted before high-risk limits are stated
dominance_rules.rule: high-risk explanations (hallucination, cutoff) wait for mechanism grounding and review
dominance_rules.required_action: block release until the limit is grounded and reviewed
dominance_rules.example: shipping a 'how it works' note that omits hallucination

dominance_rules.trigger: fluency is presented as evidence of correctness
dominance_rules.rule: never let fluent output stand in for verified truth
dominance_rules.required_action: separate fluency from truth and attach the hallucination limit

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node is wanted before its prerequisites
dominance_rules.rule: explain prerequisites before dependents regardless of perceived value

dominance_rules.trigger: a vivid analogy contradicts the actual mechanism
dominance_rules.rule: mechanism accuracy dominates when an analogy would mislead
dominance_rules.example: calling the model a database lookup

dominance_rules.trigger: a precise number is offered without a source
dominance_rules.rule: evidence labels dominate false precision; heuristic stays heuristic
dominance_rules.required_action: label estimates heuristic, avoid invented exact figures
dominance_rules.example: quoting an exact hallucination rate with no source

dominance_rules.trigger: a node is hard-locked before validation passes
dominance_rules.rule: validation dominates locking; no hard-lock before checks pass
dominance_rules.required_action: run the validator and resolve defects before locking
dominance_rules.example: locking the limits node before review

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-risk or over-trust claim could be auto-finalized
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation for high-risk explanations

dominance_rules.trigger: adding build detail would exceed the literacy altitude
dominance_rules.rule: scope altitude dominates density; defer build mechanics
dominance_rules.required_action: route build steps to the engineering subdomain

dominance_rules.trigger: output formatting would break strict JSON
dominance_rules.rule: strict JSON validity dominates prose nicety

dominance_rules.trigger: scaling or capability is stated as removing limits
dominance_rules.rule: calibration dominates hype; report gains and persistent limits together
dominance_rules.required_action: attach persistent-limit caveats to scaling claims

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the understanding-level scope before populating nodes
anti_rework_rules.rationale: nodes built at the wrong altitude are reworked when scope is set
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: build-level nodes appear before scope is fixed
anti_rework_rules.example: writing a fine-tuning how-to node first

anti_rework_rules.rationale: attention explained without vectors must be redone

anti_rework_rules.rule: explain the next-token objective before decoding/prompting/RAG
anti_rework_rules.rationale: inference explained without the distribution must be redone
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: temperature explained before the distribution exists

anti_rework_rules.rule: define each learning phase before the phase->capability map
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a map over undefined phases is reworked
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: phase map drafted before phases are defined
anti_rework_rules.example: attributing behavior with no phase definitions

anti_rework_rules.rule: explain all parts before the end-to-end pipeline trace
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a synthesis with forward references is reworked
anti_rework_rules.example: tracing decoding before decoding is defined

anti_rework_rules.rule: ground limits in mechanisms before stating them
anti_rework_rules.rationale: ungrounded limits get reworked when mechanism is added
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: limits stated with no causal mechanism
anti_rework_rules.example: hallucination claimed with no objective link

anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: scaling caveats written before limits exist

anti_rework_rules.rule: model conflict axes before dominance rules
anti_rework_rules.rationale: dominance rules over undefined conflicts are reworked
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: dominance rule with no matching conflict axis
anti_rework_rules.example: resolving a tradeoff not yet named

anti_rework_rules.rationale: locking before validation forces costly unlock
finalizing over-trust claims without review causes harmful rework

acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk and coupling
acceptance_tests: highest-risk defect is first

iteration_protocol.trigger: a fix touches a high-coupling node
iteration_protocol.detection: trace dependents and edges of the changed node
acceptance_tests: all dependents identified

iteration_protocol.detection: map failure type to its repair subsystem
acceptance_tests: each defect routed and fixed

iteration_protocol.detection: re-run the formula script over the KB
acceptance_tests: formula consistency within tolerance
overall_status pass

iteration_protocol.trigger: an evidence label or prior changed
acceptance_tests: posterior matches formula

iteration_protocol.trigger: a high-risk defect cannot be auto-repaired
iteration_protocol.detection: detect repeated failure on a risk>=0.80 node
acceptance_tests: human decision recorded

human_review_required_for: claims that fluent output is correct
attributing behavior to the wrong training phase
hard lock of the limits or objective nodes
mandatory_checks: no observed labels without observed data
semantic_checks: conflict edges signed negative with resolution rule
workflow_checks: no hard lock before validation and review
